correctness.rationale: The independent majority-success polynomial is derived by multilinearity and checked exactly at its 32 interpolation vertices. Fixed total linear term yields the A−12s²B criterion. General monotonicity follows from two optimality inequalities. For the ten-skills profile, exhaustive enumeration of all binomial(9,4)=126 unordered partitions gives A/B=(3346,6360),(3352,7710) and positive other-partition margins (36,112/3,52) at the three endpoint nodes 0,1/2700,1/900. Affine interpolation proves all-scale exclusion. Re-running packaged verifier reproduces 40 interpolation checks and 252 direct correctness-distribution checks; all exact rational. Limitations: finite verifier supplies only the finite certificate, analytic argument supplies interval conclusion.

value.rationale: The established three-person skill-product allocation rule is insensitive to uniform improvements in competence. The finding identifies five as the first odd size with genuine regrouping, gives a completely solved ten-distinct-ability example across its full continuous scale range rather than two sample points, and establishes a general monotonicity invariant governing every five-person switch. This addresses the practical model question whether scaling everyone’s reliability preserves whom to combine, without claiming empirical transfer.
